tKAEEgAAQBAJ.subtitle: The Hidden Psychology of Earning, Spending, Saving, Risk, and Building Wealth
tKAEEgAAQBAJ.summary: Why Smart People Make Bad Money Decisions examines the gap between knowing what is financially sensible and actually doing it. Intelligence does not make a person immune to inherited money rules, family history, identity, fear, status pressure, mood, habit, present bias, uncertainty, or the social meaning attached to spending. The book moves from early money lessons and the unwritten family ledger into emotional and status-sensitive purchases, lifestyle normalization, the conflict between present and future selves, opportunity cost, automation, earning power, marketable skills, confidence built from evidence, leverage, debt, risk, and the need to build a life that can survive being wrong. The final sections widen wealth beyond accumulation to relationships, financial buffers, the ability to say no, and a personal boundary for enough. A reader's notebook supplies twelve practical experiments and a decision lab uses hypothetical cases to make the psychological mechanisms visible.
tKAEEgAAQBAJ.seo_description: A practical behavioral-finance guide to inherited money rules, spending psychology, status, future-self decisions, earning power, debt, risk, financial freedom, and better money habits.
learning: Separate financial knowledge from the psychological forces that shape real decisions.
Identify inherited family rules and identity pressures that influence earning, spending, saving, and risk.
Recognize mood-driven, status-sensitive, and frictionless purchasing before it becomes a repeated pattern.
Make future tradeoffs more concrete through opportunity-cost framing, automation, and pre-decided rules.
Increase earning power by mapping valuable skills, adjacent capabilities, evidence, and leverage.
Judge financial decisions by process and risk rather than by outcome alone.
Turn debt and fragility into visible contracts, stress tests, buffers, and explicit boundaries.
Use practical experiments to define enough, strengthen the right to say no, and build quieter financial freedom.
tKAEEgAAQBAJ.target_audience: For thoughtful readers, professionals, entrepreneurs, and households who understand basic financial principles but want to understand why intelligent people still make inconsistent money decisions under pressure, habit, identity, fear, and social influence.

X6IEEgAAQBAJ.subtitle: La psicología oculta de ganar, gastar, ahorrar, asumir riesgos y crear riqueza
X6IEEgAAQBAJ.summary: Por qué las personas inteligentes toman malas decisiones financieras estudia la distancia entre saber qué decisión parece sensata y ser capaz de tomarla cuando intervienen la historia familiar, la identidad, el miedo, el estatus, el cansancio, el hábito, el presente y la incertidumbre. El libro comienza con las primeras lecciones de dinero y el libro de cuentas familiar que nadie escribió; después analiza compras emocionales y de estatus, la normalización de un nivel de gasto mayor, la relación con el yo futuro, el coste de oportunidad, el ahorro automático y la tensión entre voluntad y diseño del entorno. Más adelante pasa a la psicología de ganar más: habilidades con valor de mercado, confianza basada en pruebas, negociación y palancas. La parte de riesgo distingue una buena decisión de un buen resultado, trata la deuda como contrato antes que emoción y propone construir una vida capaz de soportar errores. El cuaderno del lector y el laboratorio de decisiones convierten las ideas en experimentos y casos hipotéticos.
X6IEEgAAQBAJ.seo_description: Guía práctica de psicología financiera sobre creencias heredadas, gasto emocional, estatus, yo futuro, ahorro, ingresos, deuda, riesgo, libertad financiera y mejores decisiones con dinero.
key_topics: Yo futuro y sesgo hacia el presente
learning: Separar el conocimiento financiero de las fuerzas psicológicas que gobiernan una decisión real.
Detectar reglas familiares heredadas e identidades que condicionan ingresos, gasto, ahorro y riesgo.
Reconocer compras emocionales, de estatus o demasiado fáciles antes de que se conviertan en hábito.
Hacer concretos los costes futuros mediante alternativas visibles, automatización y reglas previas.
Aumentar el valor de una hora desarrollando habilidades útiles, pruebas de competencia y mejores palancas.
Evaluar una decisión por su proceso y su riesgo, no solamente por el resultado.
Convertir deuda y fragilidad financiera en contratos visibles, pruebas de estrés y márgenes de seguridad.
Definir un límite personal de suficiente y usar el dinero para comprar opciones y capacidad de decir no.
X6IEEgAAQBAJ.target_audience: Para lectores, profesionales y hogares que conocen las reglas básicas de las finanzas personales pero quieren comprender por qué personas inteligentes siguen tomando decisiones inconsistentes bajo presión, hábito, identidad, miedo y comparación social.

f6IEEgAAQBAJ.subtitle: Kazanmanın, Harcamanın, Biriktirmenin, Risk Almanın ve Servet Oluşturmanın Gizli Psikolojisi
f6IEEgAAQBAJ.summary: Akıllı İnsanlar Neden Parayla İlgili Kötü Kararlar Verir?, doğru finansal kararı bilmek ile onu gerçek hayatta uygulamak arasındaki boşluğu inceler. Zekânın; aileden devralınan para kurallarına, kimlik baskısına, korkuya, statü arzusuna, ruh hâline, alışkanlıklara, bugünü geleceğe tercih etme eğilimine ve belirsizliğe karşı bağışıklık sağlamadığını gösterir. İlk para derslerinden ve kimsenin yazmadığı aile defterinden başlayarak duygusal harcamaya, cüzdandaki seyirciye, daha fazlanın normalleşmesine, gelecekteki benliğe, görünmeyen alternatife, otomasyona ve iradeye ihtiyaç duymadan önce verilen kararlara ilerler. Daha sonra beceri, kanıt, güven ve kaldıraç üzerinden daha fazla kazanmanın psikolojisini; borç, risk ve dayanıklılığı ele alır. Son bölümler serveti seçenekler, hayır diyebilme hakkı ve yeter sınırıyla ilişkilendirir; okur defteri somut deneyler sunar.
f6IEEgAAQBAJ.seo_description: Miras alınan para inançları, duygusal harcama, statü, gelecek benliği, gelir, borç, risk, finansal özgürlük ve daha iyi para kararları üzerine uygulamalı psikoloji rehberi.
learning: Finansal bilgiyi gerçek kararları yöneten psikolojik güçlerden ayırmak.
Aileden devralınan kuralları ve kimlik baskılarını fark etmek.
Duygu ve statü kaynaklı harcamaları alışkanlığa dönüşmeden tanımak.
Fırsat maliyeti, otomasyon ve önceden verilmiş kurallarla geleceği somutlaştırmak.
Beceri, kanıt ve kaldıraçla gelir gücünü artırmak.
Kararı yalnız sonucuna göre değil süreç ve risk kalitesine göre değerlendirmek.
Borç ve kırılganlığı görünür sözleşmelere, stres testlerine ve tamponlara çevirmek.
Yeter sınırını tanımlayıp parayı seçenek ve hayır diyebilme kapasitesi için kullanmak.
f6IEEgAAQBAJ.target_audience: Temel kişisel finans kurallarını bilen ama zeki insanların baskı, alışkanlık, kimlik, korku ve sosyal karşılaştırma altında neden tutarsız para kararları verdiğini anlamak isteyen okurlar, profesyoneller ve aileler için.

YKjeEQAAQBAJ.subtitle: How to Stop Undervaluing Your Time, Talent, Presence, and Life
YKjeEQAAQBAJ.summary: Wealth Begins Where You Stop Selling Yourself Cheap treats wealth as more than money and asks where a life is being quietly discounted before a price is ever named. It connects undercharging with over-explaining, unclear scope, fear of losing clients, exhausted availability, hidden talent, self-erasure in love, weak boundaries, scattered attention, and the body's record of depletion. The book also insists that apprenticeship is not humiliation and that higher prices must be supported by skill, proof, ethical value, and clean exchange rather than entitlement. Later chapters examine attention as a form of salary, panic in the marketplace, leaving without bitterness, and the difference between becoming expensive in image and accurate in life. A thirty-day repricing plan moves through observing leaks, keeping one boundary, strengthening one proof of skill, and making one cleaner exchange so self-respect becomes visible behavior rather than theory.
YKjeEQAAQBAJ.seo_description: A practical guide to self-worth, pricing, boundaries, skill, proof, attention, relationships, ethical value, and a 30-day plan for stopping the habit of selling your time and presence cheap.
learning: Recognize the nonfinancial ways a person can discount time, talent, attention, body, and presence.
Separate healthy apprenticeship from chronic underpricing or self-erasure.
Use clearer scope, boundaries, terms, and exchanges instead of fear-driven availability.
Support higher fees with stronger craft, proof, testimonials, and easier-to-understand value.
Notice how panic, over-explaining, and fear of losing a client weaken bargaining behavior.
Apply the same value logic to relationships without turning self-respect into hardness.
Treat attention and energy as scarce assets that deserve deliberate allocation.
Use a 30-day plan to turn value from an idea into repeated observable behavior.
YKjeEQAAQBAJ.target_audience: For freelancers, professionals, creators, business owners, and readers who repeatedly underprice their work, overgive time or emotional labor, struggle to state boundaries, or want a more ethical and evidence-based relationship with personal value.

DqneEQAAQBAJ.subtitle: Zamanını, Yeteneğini, Varlığını ve Hayatını Değerinin Altında Vermeyi Bırakmak
DqneEQAAQBAJ.summary: Servet, Kendini Ucuza Satmayı Bıraktığın Yerde Başlar, serveti yalnızca para olarak değil; zaman, yetenek, dikkat, beden, sınır ve yaşam alanı olarak ele alır. Kitap kişinin kendini yalnız düşük ücret kabul ettiğinde değil, yorgunken sürekli erişilebilir olduğunda, fazla açıklama yaptığında, kapsamı belirsiz tuttuğunda, müşteriyi kaybetme korkusuyla pazarlık yapamadığında, görünür olmaktan korktuğu için yeteneğini sakladığında veya ilişkide kendini sildiğinde de ucuza verebildiğini gösterir. Çıraklık ile aşağılanmayı, etik değer ile gösterişli fiyatı, beceri ile kanıtı birbirinden ayırır. Son bölümler dikkat ekonomisini, piyasa paniğini, nefret etmeden ayrılmayı ve otuz günlük yeniden fiyatlandırma planını işler: sızıntıları gözlemek, bir sınırı korumak, bir beceri kanıtını güçlendirmek ve daha temiz bir alışveriş yapmak.
DqneEQAAQBAJ.seo_description: Özdeğer, ücret, sınırlar, beceri, kanıt, dikkat, ilişkiler, etik değer ve zamanı ile varlığını ucuza vermeyi bırakmak için 30 günlük uygulama planı.
learning: Zamanı, yeteneği, dikkati, bedeni ve varlığı ucuza vermenin finans dışı biçimlerini fark etmek.
Sağlıklı çıraklık ile kronik değersizleştirmeyi ayırmak.
Korkuya dayalı erişilebilirlik yerine kapsam, sınır ve şartları netleştirmek.
Daha yüksek ücretleri beceri, kanıt, referans ve anlaşılır değerle desteklemek.
Panik ve müşteriyi kaybetme korkusunun pazarlık davranışını nasıl zayıflattığını görmek.
Özdeğer mantığını ilişkilerde sertleşmeden uygulamak.
Dikkat ve enerjiyi sınırlı varlıklar olarak korumak.
Otuz günlük planla değeri teori olmaktan çıkarıp gözlenebilir davranışa dönüştürmek.
DqneEQAAQBAJ.target_audience: İşini düşük fiyatlayan, zamanını veya duygusal emeğini fazla veren, sınır koymakta zorlanan ya da kişisel değerle daha temiz ve kanıta dayalı bir ilişki kurmak isteyen serbest çalışanlar, profesyoneller, yaratıcılar ve genel okurlar için.

GvDZEQAAQBAJ.subtitle: How Your Inner Direction Shapes Your Life, Choices, and Future
GvDZEQAAQBAJ.summary: Every Thought Is a Prayer uses prayer as a metaphor for repeated inner direction: what attention, language, habits, fear, stories, and daily choices repeatedly rehearse. Across thirteen chapters it moves from attention and dreams through self-talk, fear, habits, personal stories, realignment, inner consent, morning direction, midday correction, evening review, and the patience required when change is slow. The book explicitly avoids the claim that tragedy, illness, injustice, or loss are self-created; its narrower claim is that repeated inner agreements influence how a person meets reality and what kind of person is formed inside it. Each chapter returns to seeing the pattern, understanding direction, daily practice, and reflection. A thirty-day appendix translates the framework into small experiments involving silence, future-self writing, phone-free mornings, boundaries, difficult conversations, intentional work, inherited ambitions, and daily review.
GvDZEQAAQBAJ.seo_description: A reflective practical guide to attention, habits, self-talk, fear, inner alignment, morning direction, daily correction, reflection, and a 30-day practice for intentional living.
learning: Treat repeated attention, language, habits, and choices as directions that gradually shape identity and behavior.
Notice when a stated desire and a practiced inner direction move in opposite ways.
Recognize fear, resentment, distraction, and old stories as patterns that can be rehearsed without conscious choice.
Use morning orientation, midday correction, and evening review to interrupt inherited momentum.
Realign through small credible actions rather than dramatic declarations or perfection.
Hold personal responsibility without pretending that illness, injustice, tragedy, or loss are self-created.
Use reflection to identify old agreements, hidden loyalties, and values the calendar does not support.
Translate insight into a repeatable thirty-day practice of attention, boundaries, honest language, and intentional action.
GvDZEQAAQBAJ.target_audience: For readers drawn to reflective self-help, mindfulness, habit change, journaling, and intentional living who want a structured way to connect inner attention with visible daily choices without reducing life to simplistic positive-thinking formulas.

BsTZEQAAQBAJ.subtitle: Why Preparation Feels Like Progress—and How to Finally Act
BsTZEQAAQBAJ.summary: Do the Thing studies the distance between preparing for a life and changing it through action. It begins with respectable forms of delay: cleaner systems, more research, better tools, improved plans, public intentions, and endless readiness. It distinguishes support work from state-changing work and follows the psychology of almost through undefined goals, fear of exposure, identity built around delay, and the comfort of remaining in potential rather than contacting reality. Action is treated as the mechanism that produces feedback, reduces ambiguity, rewrites identity, and teaches the body that beginning can be survived. The middle sections develop an action psychology built around starting before certainty, finishing small things, letting clarity emerge after movement, treating motivation as a result, and using repeatable wins. The later action system becomes concrete: define one real next step, design the first ten minutes, remove friction, use cues and calendars, create bounded time containers, finish open loops, handle emotionally difficult tasks, recover quickly after interruption, and collect evidence instead of hype. The long game closes on private progress, resistance from others, self-respect through kept commitments, and a life built by what was actually done.
BsTZEQAAQBAJ.seo_description: A practical action guide to procrastination disguised as preparation, fear of exposure, starting before certainty, small completions, friction design, time containers, recovery, evidence, and self-trust.
learning: Distinguish real progress from planning, research, optimization, and organizational work that never changes the external state.
Recognize how fear of exposure and attachment to potential keep a project safely imaginary.
Use small experiments and contact with reality to generate feedback, clarity, and confidence.
Begin before feeling ready and treat motivation as something that often follows engagement.
Lower the threshold of action through tiny repeatable steps, first-ten-minute rituals, cues, and reduced friction.
Use bounded time containers and clear definitions of done to reduce open loops and increase completion.
Recover quickly after interruption instead of turning every lapse into a ceremonial restart.
Replace public identity claims with private evidence, kept commitments, and work that can be verified.
BsTZEQAAQBAJ.target_audience: For writers, creators, founders, students, professionals, and chronic over-preparers who are active around their goals but repeatedly delay the exposed, imperfect, reality-changing actions that would move the work forward.

S7fZEQAAQBAJ.subtitle: How Creativity, Beauty, Silence, and Witness Awaken the Inner Life
S7fZEQAAQBAJ.summary: Art as a Ladder to the Soul argues that creativity is not merely decoration, achievement, or entertainment but one of the forms through which a person can regain contact with an inner life thinned by speed, usefulness, performance, and constant visibility. It begins with inward fatigue, distance from one's own center, and the difference between art as escape and art as return. The book then explores why the soul needs art, creation before achievement, the forgotten language of feeling, music, drawing, writing, movement, beginnerhood, solitude, silence, beauty, numbness, and the artist as witness. Its concern is not professional artistry but the human capacity to feel, shape, witness, and offer what life is doing within. Distinct practices include listening, sketching, journaling, freewriting, movement, private dance, breath, unskilled creation, solitude, beautiful attention, thawing numbness, and ethical witness. The final movement asks the reader to protect hidden work, practice before mood, let beauty guide daily life, remain a beginner, witness what must not be lost, and carry the ladder into ordinary life.
S7fZEQAAQBAJ.seo_description: A deep practical meditation on creativity, music, drawing, writing, movement, beginnerhood, solitude, beauty, numbness, witness, and using art to return to presence and inner life.
learning: Recognize the difference between outward functioning and inward nourishment, and the role art can play in reconnecting the two.
Create before achievement by separating private practice from applause, market value, and perfection.
Use music, drawing, writing, and movement as different languages for feelings that may appear before clear explanation.
Practice beginnerhood without treating lack of skill as evidence that creativity does not belong to you.
Use solitude, silence, beauty, and attention as conditions in which inner material can ripen rather than be forced.
Work with numbness gradually through art, embodiment, tenderness, and shared feeling instead of demanding immediate drama.
Treat witnessing as an ethical practice that can hold suffering, joy, memory, community, and ordinary life without exploitation.
Build a durable creative life through small practices, hidden work, repetition, and a return to ordinary reality.
S7fZEQAAQBAJ.target_audience: For artists and non-artists alike, especially readers who feel inwardly tired, overfunctional, perfectionistic, creatively blocked, emotionally numb, or disconnected from beauty and want practical ways to use art, silence, embodiment, and witness as forms of return.
